claims.text: Overall tribo-corrosion degradation is governed by a dynamic balance between mechanical passive-film removal and electrochemical film reformation.
Mechanical wear continuously disrupts the protective passive film.
The ability to repassivate quickly after wear determines the rate of combined tribo-corrosion damage.
Phase composition, alloying, elemental partitioning, and second-phase particles influence passive-film stability.
Partitioned Cr and Ti oxides stabilize the passive film in the proposed alloys.
(AlTiV)100−xCrx alloys can have a single-phase BCC structure.
The AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy with controlled boron content is a single-phase BCC material.
The initial alloy forms a protective passive film under corrosive conditions.
Boron addition to AlCoCrFeNiMoTi-based coatings preserves BCC and sigma phases and promotes TiB2 formation and BCC refinement.
The mechanical film-removal rate is influenced by microstructural toughness.
Passive-film reformation kinetics are controlled by alloy composition and microalloying elements.
An optimum Cr content or low boron addition that enhances repassivation will lower total tribo-corrosion degradation relative to a nonoptimized baseline.
A low boron addition enhances passive-film stability and improves corrosion resistance.
The optimized alloy's wear component may increase slightly because it contains a tougher but less ductile phase.
Increasing Cr content raises hardness while reducing toughness and corrosion resistance in (AlTiV)100−xCrx alloys.
Excessive boron degrades passive-film integrity.
The prediction holds under moderate wear when passive-film removal remains within the alloy's repassivation capability.
Extreme loading or highly aggressive corrosive environments can overwhelm repassivation and cause the prediction to fail.
The quantitative relationship between passive-film removal and regrowth rates, including the effect of nanoscale boron additions on film defects, remains unresolved.
A lack of correlation between improved film reformation and reduced total degradation, or unchanged or worse degradation in the optimized alloy, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes the candidate alloy as single-phase BCC, but the AlCoCrFeNiMoTiBx example explicitly relies on sigma and TiB2 second phases as mediators; the cited evidence also identifies BCC, sigma, and TiB2 rather than a single-phase structure.
